liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Let Me In 83968** (1 review): Reviewer identifies it as from 1970-06-24, citing the instrumental licks and a crowd member's voice at the start [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **Let Me In 83968**: back after 111 archived shows (409 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [12]

## The recordings

- **gd70-08-17.aud.cotsman.12073.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 3 songs; 11 min; rated 2.8/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: This track has some channel panning and warble; Audience tapes from this period are rare and poor; this one is listenable and has some ambiance [1][6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says the venue was never officially called Fillmore West; the names were just Fillmore and Fillmore East [3]
- Graham named it Fillmore West because he had already opened Fillmore East [4]
- Reviewer says it is the early acoustic set from June 24, 1970, at the Capitol Theatre, Portchester, N.Y [10]
- The 1970-08-18 show opened with the announcer welcoming the crowd to the Fillmore West [11]
- Friend of the Devil wasn't played at the 1970-06-24 show, so the last two songs likely come from other shows [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-08-17.aud.cotsman.12073.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Chuck Gannon and JCotsman; source: Audience [1]. Also: Only a fragment of this recording circulates, and its date is uncertain; Sound Forge was used to remove several crackles and pops from the recording; Reviewer says all these songs come from Ken Lee's recording of 6/24/70, and nothing circulates from 8/17/70 [1][8][10]
